01 BOTTOM LINE

SOURCE OPINION AI inference and agent workloads drive CPU, power module and DDR5 proliferation, raising high-capacitance MLCC demand; TrendForce expects high-end MLCC shortages most severe in 1Q27-2Q27 and extending through 1H27, letting suppliers hold pricing power. C-3aa1b6d5b8b58e C-5ee7199870eb79 C-c72340c04fe402

MODEL INFERENCE High-capacitance/AI-grade MLCC suppliers such as Murata and SEMCO likely see firm or rising ASPs and favorable negotiating leverage through 1H27; the article quantifies no earnings or margin impact.

01 BOTTOM LINE

SOURCE OPINION CDS spreads on financing-dependent AI infrastructure borrowers have spiked (one weak issuer to 1,100 bps implying ~50% five-year default probability) while large cash-generative AI leaders (50-120 bps) and broad IG (~60 bps) remain comparatively contained, indicating a targeted reassessment of repayment risk for debt-reliant AI business models. ⟨cited figures: approximate; approximate, read from a chart⟩ C-50d63c69dc6db9 C-4f5d3d7ba50f80 C-bf069f4dcffacf C-d4a92cd4d83b22 C-426b0ff72b28ec C-84db623659fb1c C-56524c0cd277d4
⚠ UNRESOLVED REVIEW — Sentence states broad IG is '~60 bps' citing C-56524c0cd277d4 (investment grade around 60 bps), which is supported. The '50-120 bps' for leaders (C-50d63c69dc6db9), 1,100 bps weak issuer (C-bf069f4dcffacf), ~50% default prob (C-d4a92cd4d83b22) all supported. But the cited C-4f5d3d7ba50f80 (toward 300 bps) is not reflected and the overall claim is otherwise well-supported; minor scope mixing but defensible.
SOURCE OPINION The article suggests investors should distinguish AI issuers by their ability to finance investment, service debt and turn spending into cash flow rather than by the AI label. C-150065846631e9 C-84db623659fb1c
MODEL INFERENCE The article identifies credit-market stress as concentrated in debt-reliant AI issuers with limited cash flow; it does not quantify an earnings or equity-valuation impact for any named company, only CDS pricing and implied default probabilities.

MODEL INFERENCE A maturing Huawei-DeepSeek domestic stack could shift Chinese AI compute demand toward Ascend and away from Nvidia over time, but the article does not quantify any earnings, revenue or market-share effect for listed suppliers.

01 BOTTOM LINE

SOURCE OPINION Morgan Stanley argues Canada's potential growth could rise from ~1.5% to 1.7% by end-decade and reach 2% in the 2030s, driven by productivity, efficiency and capital deployment, supported by abundant capital (pension assets 158% of GDP), a growing working-age population (+5% by 2040), and a capex cycle in which utilities, transport, mining and energy are ~61% of planned 2026 capex. ⟨cited figures: forecast; approximate⟩ C-63741952dd42c9 C-c43a89e092cc47 C-335c33c1eb61c9 C-607b3fda6b2238 C-0b564757852ce5 C-2bb63287013c7c C-6a1792a0b1c3d9
SOURCE OPINION The payoff should be faster growth, stronger corporate earnings and a more constructive outlook for Canadian assets, including a CAD strengthening to 1.36 from ~1.39. ⟨cited figures: forecast⟩ C-0c7c6a563260f6 C-479272006058e0
MODEL INFERENCE If the capital cycle broadens from structures/engineering into machinery, software and IP and productivity spreads, Canadian corporate earnings and the Canadian dollar could benefit; the article does not quantify the earnings effect.
